PROJECT.PROJECT_TITLE: Comprehensive absolute quantitative targeted metabolomics analysis of a sweet-waxy double recessive maize mutant with enhanced kernel filling
PROJECT.PROJECT_SUMMARY: This project aims to characterize the metabolic basis for increased endosperm content in a sweet-waxy double recessive maize mutant (M4-6). Using a targeted metabolomics approach with UHPLC-QTRAP MS/MS (AB SCIEX 6500+) on HILIC and C18 columns in positive and negative ion switch mode, we quantified 337 metabolites in the endosperm of both mutant and wild-type at 20 days after pollination (n=3 per group). The mutant displayed a 41.4% increase in dry grain weight, accompanied by elevated levels of soluble sugars (43.4%) and sucrose (21.2%). Metabolomic profiling identified 68 differential metabolites (p<0.05), indicating enhanced turnover of carbon compounds, with depletion of branched-chain amino acid degradation intermediates (3-methyl-2-oxobutanoic acid, methylmalonic acid, ketoleucine, 3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid) and accumulation of metabolites such as β-alanine and tartaric acid. Pathway enrichment analysis revealed significant alterations in valine/leucine/isoleucine degradation (ko00280), glyoxylate/dicarboxylate metabolism (ko00630), and β-alanine metabolism (ko00410). This dataset provides a high-resolution metabolic profile of the mutant endosperm and offers insights into the metabolic reprogramming associated with enhanced kernel filling.

STUDY.STUDY_TITLE: Targeted metabolomics of sweet-waxy double recessive maize endosperm reveals enhanced carbon flux and amino acid degradation in a kernel-filling mutant
STUDY.STUDY_SUMMARY: This study performed a targeted, absolute quantitative metabolomics analysis on maize (Zea mays) endosperm from a sweet-waxy double recessive mutant (M4-6, n=3) and its wild-type (n=3) at 20 days after pollination (DAP). Metabolites were extracted using a cold methanol/acetonitrile/water (2:2:1, v/v) method and analyzed by UHPLC-QTRAP MS/MS (AB SCIEX 6500+) with both HILIC and C18 columns in positive and negative ion switch mode using MRM acquisition. Of the 337 metabolites quantified, 68 showed significant differences (p<0.05), with 15 upregulated and 53 downregulated in the mutant. Key findings include depletion of branched-chain amino acid degradation intermediates (3-methyl-2-oxobutanoic acid, methylmalonic acid, ketoleucine, 3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid) and accumulation of β-alanine and tartaric acid. Differential metabolites were enriched in pathways including valine/leucine/isoleucine degradation (ko00280), glyoxylate/dicarboxylate metabolism (ko00630), and β-alanine metabolism (ko00410). The results demonstrate enhanced carbon flux through catabolic pathways in the mutant endosperm.
STUDY.ADDRESS: No. 14, Xinjian North Road, Xinfu District, Xinzhou, Shanxi, 034000, China

COLLECTION.COLLECTION_SUMMARY: Maize endosperm was dissected from kernels at 20 days after pollination (DAP). Tissues were immediately frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at -80°C until metabolite extraction.

TREATMENT.TREATMENT_SUMMARY: No specific treatment was applied. The comparison is based on genotype (mutant vs wild-type).

SAMPLEPREP.SAMPLEPREP_SUMMARY: Endosperm tissue (~80 mg) was extracted with 1000 μL of cold methanol/acetonitrile/water (2:2:1, v/v). Stable-isotope internal standards were added. Samples were homogenized, sonicated, centrifuged, and the supernatant was dried under vacuum. The residue was re-dissolved in 100 μL acetonitrile/water (1:1, v/v) for LC-MS analysis.
SAMPLEPREP.EXTRACT_CLEANUP: Centrifugation at 14,000 g for 15 min at 4°C
SAMPLEPREP.SAMPLE_SPIKING: Stable-isotope labeled internal standards added during extraction

CHROMATOGRAPHY.CHROMATOGRAPHY_SUMMARY: Metabolites were separated on a C18 column (Waters UPLC BEH C18, 2.1 x 100 mm, 1.7 μm) with a gradient elution using 5 mM ammonium acetate in water (A) and 99.5% puew acetonitrile (B) at 0.4 mL/min and 40°C.
CHROMATOGRAPHY.COLUMN_NAME: Waters ACQUITY UPLC BEH C18 (100 x 2.1mm,1.7um)
CHROMATOGRAPHY.FLOW_GRADIENT: 0 min 5% B, 5 min 60% B, 11 min 100% B, 13 min 100% B, 13.1 min 5% B, 16 min 5% B

MS.MS_COMMENTS: MRM mode with positive/negative switching. Source temperature: 580°C, GS1: 45, GS2: 60, CUR: 35. IonSpray Voltage: +4500 V (positive) / -4500 V (negative). Data processed using MultiQuant software. Quantification based on stable-isotope internal standards using 1/x² weighted linear regression. MultiQuant 3.0 (AB SCIEX)
